note: Proposed, not sealed. The operator asked what has landed and what can be stripped, with a public-facing audience in view. The survey found the README at 878 lines and roughly 10 MB of the 16 MB tracked being build record rather than product. It also found that this exact trim had already been done once: tests/test_docs.py:31 says 'when the README was trimmed to a front door it moved here', and the README grew back. That is the fact this decision exists to write down, because the next survey will otherwise reach the same conclusion a third time.

decisions.question: Where does the long-form README content go on a second front-door trim — into one manual, or into topic files per section?
decisions.commitment: One file: docs/manual.md, holding the eleven sections from 'The Matcher seam' through 'Accuracy' verbatim, in their original order, with their heading text unchanged so every anchor slug survives. README drops from 878 lines to 298 and gains a 'Going further' table that routes by task rather than by feature name. The first trim distributed content to topic files (project-layout.md, matcher-seam.md, frank.md, storage-protocol.md, accuracy.md, home-paths.md) and those files stay; they are companions that go deeper than the manual's introduction, and each is linked from its section. What did NOT get another topic file is the material that had no home to go back to.
decisions.why: The distributed shape is what regrew. Eleven separate moves means eleven separate judgements about what stays behind as a summary, and a summary that stays behind is the seed of the next 878-line README — the regrowth is not sections coming back, it is introductions to sections accumulating. One file with the sections moved bodily leaves nothing behind to grow. It is also the smaller change: anchors are preserved exactly, so the only inbound links that needed rewriting were the six pointing at ../README.md#<moved-section>, and no prose was rewritten to fit a new home. The cost is a 630-line manual, which is a real cost and the honest alternative to eleven files nobody can hold in their head at once.

decisions.question: Should the build record — IDEAS.md, dogfood/, agent-log.md, archive/, audits/, bench/, scripts/corpus/, hooks/ — be deleted, moved to another repository, or kept and labelled?
decisions.commitment: Kept and labelled. docs/build-record.md draws the line, states that none of it ships (the wheel is nestor/ and the sdist adds tests/ plus four root files, both named explicitly in pyproject.toml), indexes each part with its size and what it is, and routes by the question a reader is actually asking. It closes with a section on what the record does NOT establish: that the numbers generalise, that the decisions had a second reader, or that a sealed pair is still current.
decisions.why: Deleting it is not available: 41 test files reference scripts/, 31 demo/, 20 bench/, 17 hooks/, 10 docs/dogfood/ and 5 IDEAS.md — the record is load-bearing for the gates that prove the product works, so a git rm takes the test suite with it. Moving it to a second repository breaks those same references across a boundary git does not follow. That leaves labelling, which is also the right answer on the merits rather than only the available one: for a reader deciding whether to trust a verification tool, a tool that could not show its own working would be an argument against itself. What made the 10 MB a liability was not its existence but that nothing distinguished it from the product. The 'what this does not establish' section is the part that makes it evidence rather than a brochure.

decisions.question: What has to move with content that leaves the README?
decisions.commitment: Its gates. tests/test_docs.py reads README at module scope and asserts against it; two of those assertions were about content that moved. docs/manual.md and docs/build-record.md were added to the DOCS corpus so they stay link-checked, a MANUAL constant was added beside README and LAYOUT, and test_the_readme_quotes_the_servers_refusal_verbatim was renamed to test_the_manual_quotes_... and repointed, because the PermissionError transcript it compares against nestor.serve went to the manual. The runnable-example gate stayed on README, unchanged, because the single 'Save this as `demo.py`' block is in Quick start and Quick start did not move.
decisions.why: This is the failure mode the same test file already documents twice in its own comments: 'a corpus built from ROOT.glob("*.md") alone silently stopped link-checking' the content that moved out of CLAUDE.md, and the first README trim needed matcher-seam.md, frank.md and storage-protocol.md added for the same reason. Both notes end with the word 'silently'. A doc gate that loses its subject does not fail — it passes on an empty set, which is worse than failing because nothing reports it. Verified rather than assumed: ci-docs.sh went from 59 to 61 tests when the two new files entered the corpus.
